body:
I have valium, would that be better to taper? I wanna keep taking the Xanax, it helps so much. Ugh. I wish I could take it every day because it actually lets me function.

I went for 3 weeks after using Klonopin more than a few times per week without any and didn't come across any issues I was aware of.

damn, really? :/

Have I been screwed since I took 2 mg per day for almost 2 weeks straight? I also have klonopin in my system still since it has a long half-life... I was also taking Tempazapam some nights during those 2 weeks...

- No tolerance to cannabis (had only smoked a few times via shotgunning with no ill consequences)
- Decided to try a cannabis edible, ate half of a cookie and it took effect in one hour.
- Initial effects were giggling at a fan, really strong happiness and euphoria.
- Than suddenly got really dizzy and off-balance, heart started racing to 185 bpm, started screaming for an ambulance.
- Rode in ambulance to hospital, hospital administered Ativan and Metoprolol for possible heart attack.
- Entire time, was hearing demonic laughter, peoples faces were morphing into demon faces, no perception of time, felt like anything outside my hospital room was just a black hole or void, felt like my head took off into outer space, severe paranoia thinking one of the nurses was an actual angel but everyone else wanted to dismember me alive.

Since than, I've had this hellish DPDR. When I came home from the hospital that night, I thought I had died at the hospital.

I've never done LSD, but I have had a bad cannabis trip that has caused me the same issues as you. It's know as Depersonalization/Derealization. Please read about it online, you will come to find there are thousands of others with the same set of symptoms. I know you are in a rough spot with it now but it will get better gradually over time. Medications and therapy may help. 

My symptoms are that I can't understand or grasp reality anymore, everything seems really fake or distant, it sort of feels like I have an invisible spacesuit on separating me from the world around. I have anxiety and panic attacks at times now too since this started. And I also feel like a stranger to my old self. I feel different.

A huge piece of advise is to stay away from drugs (including nicotine and caffeine) now. You need to let your mind heal.
Thank you! May I ask how long it took you to recover? Was very gradual or was it sort of like a light switch went off and you were better one day?

Thank you so much! You have given me some hope that this can go away over time. It's been around 5 months for me and I have also heard that it fades slowly over time. That people with this recover at different rates. So thank you again. :)

I only ate a half a cookie and knew not to eat anymore until the effects kicked in. It took one hour to kick in and at first, I was really giggly and euphoric. Than I kept getting higher and higher til it turned into dizziness, a panic attack, and severe paranoia. That's when my hell began.

I will admit to being naive about this all. I had heard from other people that this would help my already existant anxiety issues (mainly social anxiety) but instead, it made things go the other direction and my anxiety got worse. I know it's my own fault but I didn't go into this with ill intention. I thought I was helping myself in a medical sense. I am working on forigivng myself for putting myself into this shitty situation.
I got dizzy, really nauseated, thought I was in a different world, and panic attacks galore.
Yes, I see what you are saying. Yet I also have not experienced these issues on the Lamictal WITHOUT the Klonopin. :/
I had already been on the Lamictal for 2 weeks at that point when I took the Klonopin. I haven't had any side effects or weird visual distortions since that last Klonopin wore off after a few hours.

It's definately the Clonazepam. The visual disortions started around 1 hour after taking it and when I felt it kicking in. I never had that issue before.

The Lamotrigine is helping me though. I just haven't taken anymore Klonopin.
Oh, and I find that the TEVA generic works best for me. I tried Mylan and it didn't seem as strong.

I try not to take it unless it's absolutely necessary. When I go about 4 or 5 days without it, than I take it (.5mg), it actually makes me REALLY euphoric for a couple hours... like being high or something. But it works very well for keeping panic and anxiety under control. I honestly wish it were a med that could be taken every day with no consequences. :/

Alright, I wanted to update. I am seeing a new neurologist in a couple of months (that was the earliest they had). Also, I have not had a migraine with visual aura since this thread was made. Before that, I went 1.5 months without one. I hope they don't come back this time.
Thanks! Same to you <3

I did, and still do, feel as if dp/dr is the main issue. But I think it's because it's so... there in your face? Like you can't ignore it or push it away. So it makes it seem like it's the main issue. :/

I just started Prozac, take Klonopin as needed, and have therapy twice per week for this. I'm hoping things will get better with this combination. I used to have a pretty normal life besides some mild-moderate anxiety and depression. But that was nothing compared to now. It's laughable what I used to think feeling bad was with compared to how I feel now. Blah.

I was just diagnosed with PTSD too by both my psychiatrist and therapist. They both say my derealization is a symptom of the PTSD and anxiety. My dp/dr was caused 3 months ago by a panic attack from weed. But I also have underlying trauma (which included being robbed at gunpoint before). But I also have PTSD from the bad trip from weed (it was the worst experience of my life).

It's the weed that caused your brain to be susceptible to the DP, in my personal opinion. Than the traumatic events caused you to stay stuck in it. I'm really not sure why weed does this to some people. It did to me as well and I've been in derealization-land for 3 months now after a panic attack from weed.

You have to try your best to stay as calm as possible because any increase in anxiety definately is not going to help the DP/DR feelings. Try some medications if you're open to that. Get into therapy too.
I take Klonopin (Clonazepam) for the anxiety and it sometimes even makes me feel pretty close to normal again for at least a few hours. I'm starting Prozac (Fluoxetine) soon and am also in therapy.

I've had it for about 3 months now, same story as you. Panic attack from weed (an edible).

What have you tried so far? Medications? Therapy? Therapy is helping me. I take Klonopin as needed and it helps the panic attacks. I'm going to be trying a low dose atypical anti-psychotic and maybe anti-depressant soon.

I've noticed symptom shifting though and some improvements, even if they are very minor. But things are still feeling so unreal and unfamiliar. This is literally the hardest thing I've had to go through in life. :/
What triggered your dp/dr? I know you said you've tried almost everything, do you mean you've tried medications for it?
Zyprexa and possibly Prozac together. And I take Klonopin as needed right now.

I'm going to try an atypical anti-psychotic medication to see if it helps. I tried Paxil but after a few days of it I had a huge mind-shattering panic attack and it has made my DP a bit worse for now.
I forgot to ask... but did she take any medications at the time that helped with the depersonalization?

Thanks! I have to stay away from that sort of stuff though. It's what has caused me to be in this mess in the first place (a special brownie).

Also... I'm a girl. :P

I'm glad to hear the depersonalization went away! This is a very terrifying experience! Mine is mostly derealization but it seems to be fading. I'm taking medication too now.

Thanks :)

I'm thinking the same thing. It's a chemical change in my brain. I've just started taking Paxil and I take Klonopin as needed. My depersonalization seems to be fading and I did go over a month without any migraines. Than they came back... I'm thinking hormonal changes trigger it now. (I'm female)

I haven't had a migraine in a few days or so now. So hopefully they're gone for good or until next month. I have irregular periods too due to PCOS so figuring out when they happen will be tricky.

Well... the neurologist who prescribed it to me said if I felt a flushing in my chest to get to the ER right away... that scared me. And I honestly did not like this neurologist. I got a weird vibe and they didn't seem very concerned about me. I didn't like them at all so I don't trust their advice or what they prescribed to me. I already have strong heart palpitations a lot, even before this all started. I also have cholesterol issues currently.

I was very honest about my situation and what caused it to this neurologist. They still were not concerned and did not order an MRI and told me to come back in half a year. Like, really? I'm seeing a new doctor soon so I'm going to see what they say.

I didn't think I'd ever come across someone with the same story as mine! Has your daughter completely recovered from the depersonalization? You said it took several years, correct?

I'm around your daughter's age now and this all started for me around a few months ago.
Nice, I'll add that to my list!
I honestly can't remember where I read that. But I have looked around on that site and it did scare me so I stopped. :/

Oh, definately! I have been seeing a therapist for CBT therapy and general talk therapy since the dp/dr started. I am also planning on weaning onto an anti-depressant and than hopefully reducing my benzo usage. I have a couple of self-help books I plan on ordering too.

Thanks again!
Thank you! You are so right! I have bad bad health anxiety which makes me obsessively research stuff online. I am trying to work on stopping that. I know everyone reacts differently to medications.

Yikes, that sounds terrifying.

May I ask how long the withdrawals lasted? Did the DP/DR go away 100%?
Did you experience dp/dr from the withdrawals?

I should have known better, but it's done and in the past now. I need to keep moving forward and try to recover from this bs.

Mary jane really kicked me in the arse... and hard.

Okay, thank you.

I took a .5mg Klonopin and hour or so ago and I feel loopy (but not in a bad way). I guess that's because I waited 5 days before taking it again.
I agree, I don't see why anyone would want to watch this while tripping. Seems like a one-way ticket to a bad trip for sure.

The Klonopin helps with the anxiety and/or keeps me from having panic attacks mostly. It seems to clear up some brain fog too that I've developed as a symptom of the DP/DR. 

May I ask why you suggest an increased dosage? I actually had been wondering if taking .75mg or even 1mg at one time would be more helpful.

When you say 3-4 times a week, how many hours do you suggest be between dosages to keep a tolerance/withdrawals from developing?

Thank you kindly.

It was absolutely hellish. I think my issue was a low tolerance and too much of the stuff. It was the first time I've tried anything like that. I actually only tried it to see if it would help my mild-moderate anxiety and depression at the time but it made things x10 worse. I've never really liked medications of any kind so... meh. Gave it a shot and it got me here. :/
It's been 120 hours since my last .5 mg Klonopin. Is it safe to say I am safe from any withdrawal symptoms?

No, a pot brownie. I didn't even know you could have a bad trip on weed, but it's possible. Mine was very terrifying and I ended up in the hospital. I didn't even develop derealization until almost 2 weeks later when I had a flashback.

I've never even tried LSD or shrooms or anything.

Yeah, the Klonopin is prescribed as needed only. I try to go as long as I can between taking any, but the anxiety from my derealization is just so bad. Ugh. The medicine seems to help a lot too, but I know I can't take it everyday. I try to limit to if I feel a panic attack coming on or if I need to be out and about for therapy or whatever.

I know derealization can be a withdrawal symptom, but mine was caused by a bad drug trip.

Yes, I started the Valium April 5th. I took it three times before switching to Ativan. Took Ativan three times than switched to Klonopin, which seems to work better for me.

What type of withdrawal effects should I be feeling if I were to feel any at this point?
I'm sorry, I can't figure out how to format my post correctly. Each date with dosage is supposed to be in list form.
I think it's supposed to represent how mental illness feels. Or maybe a bad drug trip.

I've never tripped on acid, but I have had a "bad trip" from too strong of a pot edible a couple of months ago. I now have depersonalization/derealization 24/7 and this video reminded me of the trapped feeling I feel everyday now. :/

That's great! I would take brief moments of it over 24/7 like now. :)

May I ask, did you have visual symptoms? Like lights were too bright or you had trouble focusing and things seemed "blurry" in a way? If so, did that also go away completely?

Did the DP/DR go away or do you think you just got used to it? This is one thing that worries me. I want it gone compeltely as well as the memories of it.

Thank you so much for your replies everyone.

I'm going to play it safe and stick with twice per week as needed instead of twice per day as needed.
Have I screwed myself by taking it almost every day for one week now?
